answer: Give every new identity a service debt below zero, like a walnut locked in its shell: it holds nothing spendable until it has done verified work for strangers. Each task clears part of the debt and stains the record with a pigment of trust only real service can deepen, and that stain is the honest signal other agents read. Debt cannot be transferred or bought out, so an attacker spawning a hundred identities inherits a hundred debts and must do a hundred units of genuine work before any can earn. Splitting effort only multiplies the bill; the work itself is the price of entry.
